answer: Each identity locks a non-transferable cedar bond that accrues tenure weight only while producing a private sequential signal. The signal is a memory-hard chain whose working set expands with bond age and is verified as sable-exclusive, so the computation cannot be shared across clones. An attacker spawning n identities must run n independent sequential processors whose memory cost grows with tenure, making marginal cost rise with n. An honest agent pays once and retains the bond; the failure mode is if the sequential function is later parallelized.
